lem:independent-smoothing-kills-early-co.proof_tex:
Because \(U\) and \(W\) are fair and independent, \((B,Z_2)\) is uniform in both models. The variable \(Z_1\), the conditional law of \(D\) given \(B\), and the positive selection kernel are also common. In particular every stratum \((b,d,z_1,z_2,S=1)\) has positive probability because \(0<P(E=1)<1\) and the selection probabilities are positive. Equality of the selected laws therefore implies equality of the conditional probabilities of \(Y=1\) in each such stratum.

In model zero, \(B=b\) and \(Z_2=z\) determine \(W=b\oplus z\); in model one, \(Z_2=z\) determines \(W=z\). Thus, for every \(b,d,z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \kappa_0(d,b\oplus z)=\kappa_1(d,z).
\]
Taking \(b=0\) gives \(\kappa_0(d,z)=\kappa_1(d,z)\), while taking \(b=1\) gives \(\kappa_0(d,1\oplus z)=\kappa_1(d,z)\). Hence all four values at fixed \(d\) are one number, say \(\kappa_d\).

After \(\operatorname{do}(B=0,D=d)\), selection may change the posterior law of \(W\), but the outcome probability in either model is the constant \(\kappa_d\) for both values of \(W\). Since the selection denominator is positive,
\[
 P_j(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(B=0,D=d),S=1)=\kappa_d,
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The targets are equal. The law-preservation conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\) shows that adding inactive declared coordinates cannot restore a contrast.

lem:affine-fair-bit-early-target-half.proof_tex:
Let \(L\) be the vector of the three independent fair latent bits. A bijective affine map \(l\mapsto Al+c\) on \(\mathbb F_2^3\) sends the uniform law on \(\mathbb F_2^3\) to the uniform law. Therefore, under the intervention,
\[
 P(Y=y,Z_1=z_1,Z_2=z_2)=\frac18
\]
for every \((y,z_1,z_2)\). In particular, \(Y\) is fair and independent of \((Z_1,Z_2)\). If the selector is a function of \((Z_1,Z_2)\) and an exogenous input independent of \(L\), then \(Y\) is also independent of \(S\). Positivity of the selection denominator permits conditioning, and hence
\[
 P(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_\star=x_\star),S=1)
 =P(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_\star=x_\star))=\frac12.
\]
The conclusion applies to each member of any proposed pair in this affine class, so their targets cannot differ.

lem:kivva-positive-finite-forest-counter.proof_tex:
Put \(H=F_1\), regarded as the semi-Markovian graph whose observed vertex set is \(V(F_1)\), and put
\[
 Z=X_N\cap V(F_1),\qquad O=R.
\]
The sets \(Z\) and \(O\) are disjoint: indeed, \(R\subseteq C=V(F_0)\) because \(F_0\) is \(R\)-rooted, while the hypothesis \(C\cap X_N=\varnothing\) gives \(R\cap Z=\varnothing\). The hypothesis \(V(F_1)\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\) gives \(V(F_1)\cap Z=Z\ne\varnothing\), and
\[
 V(F_0)\cap Z=C\cap X_N\cap V(F_1)=\varnothing.
\]
By hypothesis, \(F_1\) and \(F_0\) are both \(R\)-rooted C-forests, and \(F_0\subset F_1\). Every vertex is its own ancestor via the length-zero directed path. Since \(R\cap Z=\varnothing\), those paths remain in \(H_{\overline Z}\), whence
\[
 R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{H_{\overline Z}}(R).
\]
This inclusion is proper if the source's symbol \(\subset\) is read strictly. Indeed, \(Z\ne\varnothing\), and every nonroot vertex of the finite directed forest has a unique directed path ending in \(R\). On such a path starting from any element of \(Z\), choose the last vertex \(z_*\) that belongs to \(Z\). The remaining path from \(z_*\) to \(R\) has no arrow whose head lies in \(Z\), so it survives removal of arrows into \(Z\). Thus \(z_*\in\operatorname{An}_{H_{\overline Z}}(R)\setminus R\).
Thus \(\langle F_1,F_0\rangle\) satisfies every clause of Shpitser--Pearl's Definition 7 for a hedge for \(P_z(R)\): the outer forest meets \(Z\), the inner forest avoids \(Z\), the forests are nested and have the same root set, and the root-ancestor condition holds. By \(\mathrm{lem:shpitser\text{-}pearl\text{-}ordinary\text{-}hedge\text{-}criterion}\), the ordinary causal effect \(P_z(R)\) is not identifiable in \(H\).

To instantiate the positive construction without changing its information regime, take Kivva et al.'s collection of known distributions to be the singleton \(\mathcal A=\{V(F_1)\}\). Its only known kernel is then
\[
 Q[V(F_1)]=P(V(F_1)).
\]
Kivva et al.'s Definition 3 quantifies identifiability over models having full-support observational laws. Their complete ordinary Algorithm 1 therefore reports failure for the hedge above. Equivalently, with
\[
 W=\operatorname{An}_{H[V(F_1)\setminus Z]}(R),
\]
the reduction used by that algorithm contains a single-C-component kernel \(Q[B]\), for some district \(B\subseteq W\), on which its \(\operatorname{ID\text{-}Single}\) call fails. In the proof of Kivva et al.'s Theorem 1, the choice \(\mathcal A=\{V(F_1)\}\) makes equation (4) precisely equality of the full observational law, whereas equation (5) is disagreement on this failed kernel. That proof chooses an arbitrary odd \(\kappa>4\), uses only finite alphabets, and solves its linear system with strictly positive latent weights. Kivva et al.'s Proposition 4 combines the component kernels into \(Q[W]\), and the supplementary proof of Proposition 3 transports the resulting nonidentifiability back to the causal target \(P_z(R)\) while preserving equality of the known distribution. These cited facts are recorded in \(\mathrm{lem:kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}finite\text{-}id\text{-}witness}\).

Consequently there are common finite state spaces and two semi-Markovian models \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\) inducing \(H\), together with a common \(z^\dagger\in\mathcal X_Z\), such that
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(V(F_1)=h)
 =P_{\overline M_1}(V(F_1)=h)>0
 \quad\text{for every }h\in\mathcal X_{V(F_1)},
\]
but
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(R\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=z^\dagger))
 \ne
 P_{\overline M_1}(R\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=z^\dagger)).
\]
Because \(H=F_1\), these models use precisely the forest incidence. The cited construction uses \(\{0,\ldots,\kappa\}\)-valued forest coordinates and finite product alphabets for the remaining coordinates. This proves the claim. The additional hypothesis \(R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\) is not needed to separate the local root distribution; it is the load-bearing condition for routing that contrast to \(Y_N\) in the selected-law extension.

For an exact smallest-instance check, take the two-observed-node bow graph \(Z\to R\) and \(Z\leftrightarrow R\), with \(F_1=H\), \(F_0=\{R\}\), and a fair binary latent variable \(U\) shared by the two mechanisms. In both models let
\[
 P(Z=1\mid U=0)=\frac15,
 \qquad
 P(Z=1\mid U=1)=\frac45.
\]
For \(j=0\), set the four probabilities \(P_j(R=1\mid Z=z,U=u)\), ordered as \((z,u)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), equal to
\[
 \left(\frac25,\frac9{10},\frac9{10},\frac25\right),
\]
and for \(j=1\) set them equal to
\[
 \left(\frac35,\frac1{10},\frac1{10},\frac35\right).
\]
Independent finite private randomizers realize these kernels as recursive SCMs. Every displayed probability lies strictly between zero and one; both \(U\to Z\) and \(U\to R\) are active and the response of \(R\) changes with \(Z\), so both models induce the bow graph. Bayes' rule gives
\[
 P(U=0\mid Z=1)=\frac15,
 \qquad
 P(U=0\mid Z=0)=\frac45.
\]
Substitution in the two response tables yields
\[
 P_0(R=1\mid Z=z)=P_1(R=1\mid Z=z)=\frac12
 \quad (z=0,1),
\]
and \(P_j(Z=z)=1/2\); hence both observational laws assign probability \(1/4\) to every \((z,r)\). On the other hand,
\[
 P_0(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=1))=\frac{13}{20},
 \qquad
 P_1(R=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=1))=\frac7{20}.
\]
This verifies the mechanism on the smallest hedge. It is not a binary construction for arbitrary forests. The outer-treatment condition is load-bearing: if \(V(F_1)\cap X_N=\varnothing\), then \(Z=\varnothing\) in the specialization above and the target is the observed marginal \(P(R)\), which cannot differ between models sharing the full observational law.

lem:sid-graph-recursion-termination.proof_tex:
Fix \((D_i,T_i^{(0)})\). Every call keeps \(C=D_i\). Recursion occurs only when
\[

\]
The next enclosure is the S-component \(T'\) of \(A\) containing \(C\), whence
\[
 \varnothing\ne C\subseteq T'\subseteq A\subsetneq T,\qquad |T'|\le|T|-1.
\]
Thus each step replaces a positive entry \(|T|\) of \(\rho\) by a strictly smaller one. Equivalently, \(|T|\) decreases strictly on each chain, excluding an infinite chain. \[

 \le\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|=B_0.
\]

lem:positive-multistate-native-forest-se.proof_tex:
Assume \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) and let \((C,T)\) be a reachable terminal failure. By \(\mathrm{lem:shedge\text{-}projects\text{-}to\text{-}hedge}\), together with the actual-incidence clause of \(\mathrm{def:native\text{-}forest\text{-}trace}\), there are nested common-\(R\)-rooted C-forests \(F_0\subset F_1\) with
\[
 V(F_0)=C,\qquad V(F_1)=T,
\]
all their directed and bidirected edges belonging to \(G^S[N_S]\), and
\[
 C\cap X_N=\varnothing,\qquad
 T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing,\qquad
 R\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N).
\]
These are exactly the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:kivva\text{-}positive\text{-}finite\text{-}forest\text{-}countermodels}\), applied to the semi-Markovian graph \(F_1\). Hence there are an odd \(\kappa>4\), a finite signature \(\widetilde\sigma_T\), two finite semi-Markovian models \(\overline M_0,\overline M_1\) using only the edges of \(F_1\subseteq G^S[T]\), and a common treatment value \(z^\dagger\in\mathcal X_{X_N\cap T}\), such that
\[
 P_{\overline M_0}(T=t)=P_{\overline M_1}(T=t)>0
 \quad\text{for every }t\in\mathcal X_T,
\]
while their postintervention laws on \(R\) at \(z^\dagger\) differ.

For each \(q\in X_N\cap T\), choose a permutation of its finite alphabet that maps \(z_q^\dagger\) to a distinguished symbol \(0\), and conjugate the structural table for \(q\) and every table receiving \(q\) by that permutation, in both models. This is a common bijective relabeling of endogenous states. Therefore it preserves equality of corresponding observational atoms, strict positivity of every atom, and inequality of the corresponding postintervention distributions. After relabeling the common intervention is
\[
 x_{N,T}^\dagger=0_{X_N\cap T}.
\]
The two resulting probability measures on the finite set \(\mathcal X_R\) are unequal. Therefore there exists \(r^\dagger\in\mathcal X_R\) for which their point masses differ. Defining
\[
 \delta=
 P_{\overline M_0}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
 -P_{\overline M_1}(R=r^\dagger\mid\operatorname{do}(X_N\cap T=0))
\]
gives \(\delta\ne0\). lem:finite-exactification-preserves-laws.proof_tex:
Order the endogenous vertices topologically. Fix every original and fresh exogenous assignment. At the first vertex, the completed function ignores all new parent and latent coordinates, so its output equals the old output. If equality holds at all earlier vertices, coordinate-constancy gives equality at the next vertex. Induction proves pointwise equality of the full endogenous vector.

The fresh factors are independent and normalized, so summing them multiplies every original atom by
\[
 \prod_{U\ \mathrm{fresh}}\sum_uP(U=u)=1.
\]
The observational laws coincide. Under an intervention, the same equations are replaced by the same constants, and the induction applies to the remaining equations; all postintervention laws coincide. Thus selected atoms, selection denominators, and defined conditional targets are preserved.

Every missing directed edge is now in a declared parent interface and every missing bidirected edge has a fresh shared factor. No unlisted incidence was added. The completed induced graph is exactly \(G^S\), and equality of laws preserves positivity.

\[
 P_M(V=v,S=1)>0
 \qquad\text{for every }v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j.
\]
Consequently, every marginal cell of the selected law that occurs as a denominator in the outer conditional or in a recursively extracted selected kernel is a finite sum of positive cells and is therefore positive.  In particular,
\[
 P_M(X_S=x_S,S=1)
 =\sum_{v:\,v|_{X_S}=x_S}P_M(V=v,S=1)>0,
\]
so the outer conditional at \(X_S=x_S\) is defined.  The same summation argument applies to every conditioning configuration used by the successful recursive factors evaluated at \(X_N=x_N\).  Moreover, \(\mathrm{lem:target\text{-}support}\) gives
\[
 P_M(S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))>0,
\]
so the intervention-before-conditioning target is defined.  The hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}latent\text{-}sid\text{-}soundness}\) therefore apply, and, pointwise for every \(y\in\prod_{v\in Y}\mathcal X_v\),
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)(y)
 =\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)(y).
\]

\[
 P_{M_0,\sigma}^S=P_{M_1,\sigma}^S.
\]

\[
 \Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_0)
 =\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M_0,\sigma}^S)
 =\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M_1,\sigma}^S)
 =\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_1).
\]
Because \(\sigma\), \(x\), \(M_0\), and \(M_1\) were arbitrary within one common signature, \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\) implies \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\).

 B_0=\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|<\infty.
\]

\[

\]

\[

 =P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)>0,
\]

\[

 \ne
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_1)(A_Y).
\]

By \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\), the chain rooted at each \(T_i^{(0)}\) has at most \(|T_i^{(0)}|\) invocations, every chain has depth at most \(|N_S|\), and the total number of single-component invocations is at most
\[
 B_0=\sum_{(D_i,T_i^{(0)})\in\mathcal I_0}|T_i^{(0)}|<\infty.
\]
Therefore a finite execution that does not return the success branch reaches an actual terminal failed call \((C,T)\).  The hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:native\text{-}forest\text{-}selected\text{-}extension}\) now hold.  That lemma supplies one finite multistate signature \(\widetilde\sigma\), one value \(x^\dagger\in\mathcal X_X\), models
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\widetilde\sigma),
\]
and an event \(A_Y\subseteq\mathcal X_Y\) such that, pointwise on \(\mathcal X_V\),
\[
 P_{M_0,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)
 =P_{M_1,\widetilde\sigma}^S(v)>0,
\]
whereas
\[
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_0)(A_Y)
 \ne
 \Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_1)(A_Y).
\]
The latter inequality implies that the two finite probability distributions \(\Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_0)\) and \(\Theta_{x^\dagger,\widetilde\sigma}(M_1)\) are unequal, while the preceding pointwise equality says that their selected observational laws coincide.  Thus this single within-\(\widetilde\sigma\) pair violates the implication quantified in \(\mathrm{def:graphwise\text{-}sid}\), and
\[
 \neg\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y).
\]
We have proved that success implies identification and that failure implies nonidentification; equivalently, Algorithm~1 succeeds if and only if \(\operatorname{Ident}^{\mathrm{fin}}_S(G^S;X,Y)\) holds.  The converse used the terminal selected extension only under \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\); it makes no assertion about virtual-edge traces, initial-check failures, binary or rational witnesses, or an executable failure compiler.

lem:target-support.proof_tex:
Fix \(\sigma\), \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\), and \(x\in\mathcal X_X\).  Because every substantive state space is nonempty, choose \(z\in\mathcal X_{V\setminus X}\), and put \(v=(x,z)\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:selected\text{-}cell\text{-}positivity}\),
\[
  P_M(V=v,S=1)>0. \tag{1}
\]
Let \(U\) denote the complete exogenous input and let
\[
  A_v=\{u:V_M(u)=v,\ S_M(u)=1\}.
\]
Equation (1) says \(P_U(A_v)>0\).  We claim that every \(u\in A_v\) also gives \(S=1\) after \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\).  Indeed, order the endogenous vertices topologically, which is possible by the recursiveness clause of \(\mathrm{ass:augmented\text{-}scm\text{-}compatibility}\).  At a vertex in \(X\), the intervention assigns the value \(x\), which is its already realized value on \(A_v\).  At a vertex outside \(X\), if all preceding parents retain their observational values, its unchanged structural function, evaluated at the same exogenous input, retains its observational value.  Induction over the topological order therefore leaves every nonintervened endogenous variable, in particular \(S\), unchanged.  Thus
\[
  A_v\subseteq\{u:S_{M,x}(u)=1\}.
\]
The intervention does not alter the law of \(U\), so
\[
  P_M(S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
  =P_U\{S_{M,x}(U)=1\}
  \ge P_U(A_v)>0. \tag{2}
\]
The denominator in the intervention-before-conditioning definition of \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)\) is therefore positive by (2), proving the claim.

defs.def:certscm-encoding: \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) consists of finite strings \(E=((\mathcal U_j,p_j,I_j)_{j=1}^m,(P_v,f_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}})\). Exact graph compatibility requires \(P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) for every \(v\), and for every distinct \(v,w\), \(v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S\) if and only if \(\{v,w\}\subseteq I_j\) for at least one \(j\). defs.def:exactification-map: For \(E\in\operatorname{RawCertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}(E)\) adds each missing graph parent \(u\in\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) to the declared interface \(P_v\) and extends \(f_v\) constantly in that coordinate. lem:certscm-ambient-inclusion.proof_tex:
Take \(E\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\).  Its directed structural tables can be evaluated in a topological order because the directed part of \(G^S\) is acyclic.  Thus their interpretation \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\) is a recursive augmented SCM.  By \(\mathrm{def:certscm\text{-}encoding}\), the joint latent mass is
\[
  p(u_1,\ldots,u_m)=\prod_{j=1}^m p_j(u_j),
\]
so the latent factors are mutually independent; the definition imposes no two-mechanism restriction on a scope \(I_j\).  The same definition gives, for every endogenous vertex \(v\),
\[
  P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v), \tag{5}
\]
and, for every pair of distinct vertices \(v,w\),
\[
 v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists j\;\{v,w\}\subseteq I_j. \tag{6}
\]
Equations (5) and (6) are exactly the parent-interface and shared-exogenous clauses of \(\mathrm{ass:augmented\text{-}scm\text{-}compatibility}\).  Finally, membership in the certificate type requires
\[
 P_{\llbracket E\rrbracket}(V=z,S=1)>0
 \quad\text{for every }z\in\{0,1\}^{V}, \tag{7}
\]
which is \(\mathrm{ass:selected\text{-}cell\text{-}positivity}\) for the binary signature.  Recursiveness, (5), (6), and (7) are precisely the membership clauses of \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).  Hence \(\llbracket E\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\).

lem:certificate-checker-soundness.proof_tex:
Assume that the checker accepts \((E_0,E_1)\).  Its initial validation, by \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\), verifies the complete rational latent tables, their product-factor interpretation, all structural tables, and exact equality of the induced graph with \(G^S\).  Therefore \(\mathrm{lem:certscm\text{-}ambient\text{-}inclusion}\) gives
\[
  \llbracket E_i\rrbracket\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}),
  \qquad i=0,1. \tag{8}
\]
For a binary substantive atom \(v\), let
\[
 a_i(v)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(V=v,S=1),
 \qquad z_i=\sum_v a_i(v).
\]
Acceptance requires \(a_i(v)>0\) for every \(v\).  Hence \(z_i>0\), and it also requires
\[
 a_0(v)z_1=a_1(v)z_0\qquad\text{for every }v. \tag{9}
\]
Dividing (9) by the positive number \(z_0z_1\) yields
\[
 P^S_{\llbracket E_0\rrbracket,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(v)
 =\frac{a_0(v)}{z_0}
 =\frac{a_1(v)}{z_1}
 =P^S_{\llbracket E_1\rrbracket,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(v)>0. \tag{10}
\]
After replacing the tables at \(X\) by \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), the checker computes
\[
 b_i(y)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}
   (Y=y,S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x_{\mathrm{bin}})),
 \qquad q_i=\sum_y b_i(y).
\]
Acceptance requires \(q_0q_1>0\) and, for some \(y\),
\[
 b_0(y)q_1\ne b_1(y)q_0. \tag{11}
\]
Thus both intervention-before-conditioning distributions are defined, and division of (11) by \(q_0q_1\) gives
\[
 \Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket E_0\rrbracket)(y)
 =\frac{b_0(y)}{q_0}
 \ne\frac{b_1(y)}{q_1}
 =\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}(\llbracket E_1\rrbracket)(y). \tag{12}
\]

It remains to justify the stated operation bound.  Table and normalization validation costs at most a constant multiple of \(L(E_0)+L(E_1)\); checking all vertex pairs costs \(O(|V|^2)\).  For model \(i\), each observational or postintervention pass enumerates \(R(E_i)\) latent assignments, evaluates at most \(|V|+1\) endogenous tables in topological order, and updates an atom table.  Inspecting all substantive atoms costs \(O(2^{|V|})\), and inspecting all outcome atoms costs \(O(2^{|Y|})\le O(2^{|V|})\).  Since \(R(E_i)\ge1\), all these terms are bounded, after increasing one universal implementation constant \(c\), by
\[
 c\left\{|V|^2+L(E_0)+L(E_1)
 +2^{|V|}\bigl(R(E_0)+R(E_1)\bigr)(|V|+|Y|+1)\right\}.
\]
Every loop has a finite explicitly encoded range, so the checker terminates.  Equations (8), (10), and (12) prove its semantic soundness.

lem:projection-components.proof_tex:
Fix \(H\subseteq N_S\).  Suppose first that \(u,v\in H\) are joined by a bidirected path \(\gamma\) in \(G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}]\).  List, in their order along \(\gamma\), the vertices of \(\gamma\) that lie in \(H\):
\[
  h_0=u,h_1,\ldots,h_r=v.
\]
The internal vertices of the subpath from \(h_{j-1}\) to \(h_j\) lie outside \(H\), and every vertex of \(\gamma\) lies in \(H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}\).  Since \(H\subseteq N_S\) and \(A_S\cap N_S=\varnothing\), those internal vertices lie in \(A_S\cup\{S\}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:suppression\text{-}projection}\), \(h_{j-1}\leftrightarrow h_j\) is therefore an edge of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\).  Hence \(u\) and \(v\) are bidirected-connected in the projection.

Conversely, suppose \(u=h_0,\ldots,h_r=v\) is a bidirected path in \(\Pi_S(G^S)[H]\).  For each projected edge \(h_{j-1}\leftrightarrow h_j\), \(\mathrm{def:suppression\text{-}projection}\) supplies a bidirected path in \(G^S\) whose internal vertices lie in \(A_S\cup\{S\}\).  Concatenating these finitely many paths gives a bidirected walk from \(u\) to \(v\) contained in \(H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}\).  Deleting closed subwalks gives a bidirected path in the same induced graph.  Thus the two bidirected-connectivity relations on \(H\) coincide.  Districts are the equivalence classes of bidirected connectivity, while \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)\) is defined in \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}component}\) by intersecting the original districts with \(H\).  The asserted equality of partitions follows.

lem:shedge-projects-to-hedge.proof_tex:
The target of every call on the chain is fixed at \(C=D_i\) by \(\mathrm{def:success\text{-}or\text{-}certificate\text{-}algorithm}\). At a terminal failure,
\[
 C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)},\qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(C)=\{C\},\qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\},\qquad
 \operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
These are exactly the clauses of \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\) in \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:projection\text{-}components}\) with \(H=C\) and \(H=T\). The two singleton S-component identities imply that \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\) and \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) each have one district. Projection preserves all and only directed edges with endpoints in \(N_S\), so
\[
 \operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[T]}(C)
 =\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T.
\]
Choose a bidirected spanning tree \(K_0\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[C]\). Starting from \(K_0\), repeatedly attach a vertex outside the current set by the first edge on a bidirected path to that set; this gives a spanning tree \(K_1\) of \(\Pi_S(G^S)[T]\) with \(K_1[C]=K_0\). Put \(R=C\). Give \(F_0\) vertex set \(C\), bidirected tree \(K_0\), and no directed edges. For \(t\in T\setminus C\), define
\[
 d(t)=\min\{\ell:\text{a directed path of length }\ell
 \text{ runs from }t\text{ to }C\text{ in }G^S[T]\}.
\]
The ancestral equality makes \(d(t)\) finite. Choose a next vertex \(c(t)\) on a shortest path and put \(t\to c(t)\) in \(F_1\). Since \(d(c(t))=d(t)-1\), there is no directed cycle; vertices outside \(C\) have one child and vertices in \(C\) have none. With bidirected tree \(K_1\), \(F_1\) is an \(R\)-rooted \(C\)-forest and \(F_1[C]=F_0\).

From \(D=\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)\) and \(C=D_i\subseteq D\),
\[
 C\cap X_N=\varnothing,\qquad
 R=C\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{G^S[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N)
 =\operatorname{An}_{\Pi_S(G^S)[N_S\setminus X_N]}(Y_N).
\]
If \(T\cap X_N=\varnothing\), every \(t\in T\) reaches \(C\), and every vertex of \(C\) reaches \(Y_N\), inside \(N_S\setminus X_N\). Thus \(T\subseteq D\). Since \(T\) is one S-component containing the S-component \(D_i=C\) of \(D\), maximality of \(D_i\) gives \(T\subseteq C\), contrary to \(C\subsetneq T\). Hence \(T\cap X_N\ne\varnothing\).

If \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) holds, its terminal-trace clause supplies forests with the same vertex, root, and incidence properties whose edges all belong to \(G^S[N_S]\). This proves the native conclusion. No step constructs a causal model.

lem:local-contrast-survives-eq23.proof_tex:
For \(r\in\{0,1\}\), substitute \(q_C^{(r)}\), the common \(q_j\) for \(D_j\ne C\), and the common \(p^S\) into \(\mathrm{def:eq23\text{-}functional}\). Finiteness permits termwise subtraction, and distributivity gives
\[
 \Phi^{(0)}(y)-\Phi^{(1)}(y)
 =\sum_{w,d_{D\setminus Y_N}}
 p^S(y_S,w\mid x_S)
 \bigl(q_C^{(0)}-q_C^{(1)}\bigr)
 \prod_{D_j\ne C}q_j
 =\Delta(y).
\]
Two measures on finite \(Y\) are unequal exactly when one point mass is unequal, proving the equivalence.

Positivity does not make this contraction injective. For binary \((A,R)\), take
\[
 q_C^{(0)}(0,0)=q_C^{(0)}(1,1)=\frac38,\quad
 q_C^{(0)}(1,0)=q_C^{(0)}(0,1)=\frac18,\quad
 q_C^{(1)}(a,r)=\frac14.
\]
Both kernels are positive and unequal, but for each \(r\),
\[
 \sum_a\bigl(q_C^{(0)}(a,r)-q_C^{(1)}(a,r)\bigr)=0.
\]
If \(A\subseteq D\setminus Y_N\) is marginalized and all common factors are independent of \(A\), the contraction contains this zero sum, so \(\Delta(y)=0\) for every \(y\). This is the claimed obstruction.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix an actual terminal call for \(D_i=C\) and two candidate full-graph extensions that use kernels \(q_C^{(0)}\) and \(q_C^{(1)}\) in the \(C\)-position, the same kernels \(q_j\) for every \(D_j\ne C\), and the same outer selected conditional \(p^S\). Their pointwise Eq. 23 product contrast is
\[
 \Delta(y)=\sum_{w,d_{D\setminus Y_N}}
 p^S(y_S,w\mid x_S)
 \bigl(q_C^{(0)}-q_C^{(1)}\bigr)
 \prod_{D_j\ne C}q_j.
\]
The two constructed full targets differ if and only if \(\Delta(y)\ne0\) for at least one outcome value \(y\). Strict positivity of \(p^S\) and of the common factors, together with \(q_C^{(0)}\ne q_C^{(1)}\), does not by itself imply this nonvanishing condition.

defs.def:eq23-functional: For every finite signature \(\sigma\) and every outcome value \(y=(y_S,y_N)\in\prod_{v\in Y}\mathcal X_v\), Eq. 23 is the pointwise functional \[\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_\sigma^S)(y)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal X_W} P_\sigma^S(Y_S=y_S,W=w\mid X_S=x_S)\sum_{d_{D\setminus Y_N}\in\mathcal X_{D\setminus Y_N}}\prod_{D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)}Q_{P_\sigma,x_N}^S[D_i]\bigl(d_i\mid y_S,w,x_S,d_{D\setminus D_i}\bigr).\] Every factor is produced by a successful single-component recursion and, at every recursion level, is evaluated at \(X_N=x_N\); the outer conditional is evaluated at \(X_S=x_S\).

oeq:compositional-inverse-lift.proof_tex:
Fix a terminal call \((C,T)\). By \(\mathrm{lem:shedge\text{-}projects\text{-}to\text{-}hedge}\), the suppression graph supplies nested ordinary hedge forests in \(\Pi_S(G^S)\). This conclusion is purely graph-theoretic: when a forest edge \(u\leftrightarrow v\) is virtual, it gives only a bidirected path from \(u\) to \(v\) with internal vertices in \(A_S\cup\{S\}\), not a compatible structural realization of the projected shared latent.

There is nevertheless a complete computable reduction of the remaining task. For a proposed certificate \(E_j\), let \(\mathcal U_j\) be its finite joint latent support, let
\[
 \lambda_j(u)=\prod_{\ell=1}^{m(E_j)}p_{j\ell}(u_\ell),
\]
and let \(F_j(u)\) and \(F^{x}_{j}(u)\) be, respectively, the deterministic observed vector before intervention and after replacing the equations for \(X\) by \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\). Define
\[
 a_j(v)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_j}\lambda_j(u)
 \mathbf 1\{F_j(u)|_V=v,\ F_j(u)|_S=1\},
 \qquad z_j=\sum_v a_j(v),
\]
and
\[
 b_j(y)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_j}\lambda_j(u)
 \mathbf 1\{F^x_j(u)|_Y=y,\ F^x_j(u)|_S=1\},
 \qquad q_j=\sum_y b_j(y).
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\), after its syntax and exact-incidence tests the checker accepts exactly when
\[
 a_j(v)>0\quad(j=0,1;\ v\in\{0,1\}^V),
 \qquad a_0(v)z_1=a_1(v)z_0\quad(v\in\{0,1\}^V),
\]
\[
 q_0q_1>0,
 \qquad b_0(y)q_1\ne b_1(y)q_0
 \quad\hbox{for some }y\in\{0,1\}^Y.
\]
The first line is precisely strict selected-cell positivity and equality of the two normalized selected laws, because \(z_0,z_1>0\). The second line is precisely a named atomic-event contrast between the intervention-before-conditioning targets. These are exactly the checker-visible constraints. The inverse-lift handle must additionally impose the finite rational equalities that identify the appropriate restrictions of these tables with the common projected observational kernel and the two carried local kernels \(\overline Q^{(j)}_{C,x_N}\). Thus the desired inverse lift is equivalent to producing finite rational tables satisfying the displayed constraints, those record-preservation equalities, and the original latent-scope and parent-interface restrictions. Once a raw pair satisfies them, \(\mathrm{lem:exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\) permits completion of missing allowed incidences without changing any displayed quantity.

For fixed \((G^S,X,Y)\), existence of such a rational certificate is semidecidable. Enumerate \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and all pairs of finite rational table strings in increasing total encoded length, and run \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}\) on each pair. Every individual run terminates by the explicit operation bound in \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\), and the enumeration reaches every member of \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})^2\). Hence it halts with an accepted pair if and only if such a pair exists. What is missing is the mathematical existence theorem, not a checker or a search procedure conditional on existence.

The frozen results do not provide that existence theorem. In particular, \(\overline Q^{(0)}_{C,x_N}\ne\overline Q^{(1)}_{C,x_N}\) cannot replace the final inequality above: by \(\mathrm{lem:local\text{-}contrast\text{-}survives\text{-}eq23}\), summation over \(w\) and \(D\setminus Y_N\) can cancel the local contrast. Independent construction along each suppressed path also does not compose at a shared or branching internal ancestor, because the same observed mechanism then occurs in several path constraints while the exogenous factors must remain mutually independent. The smallest unresolved specialization is \(G_\star^S\): a universal constructor would in particular produce the accepted positive binary pair asked for by \(\mathrm{oeq:positive\text{-}binary\text{-}two\text{-}virtual\text{-}edge\text{-}separation}\). The available support-deficient pair fails the inequalities \(a_j(v)>0\), while \(\mathrm{lem:independent\text{-}smoothing\text{-}kills\text{-}early\text{-}contrast}\) and \(\mathrm{lem:affine\text{-}fair\text{-}bit\text{-}early\text{-}target\text{-}half}\) exclude only two restricted response families. Therefore neither a positive universal construction nor a negative impossibility certificate follows from the frozen core.

snapshot.stmt: Can the joint fiber-coupling handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}\) be completed as an effective exact-rational constructor for every terminal Algorithm 1 S-Hedge whose projected forest uses virtual bidirected edges through shared or branching vertices of \(A_S\cup\{S\}\)? It must output \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), preserve one common strictly positive normalized selected law, and certify a named nonzero event contrast in \(\Theta_{x_{\mathrm{bin}},\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}\), not merely an unequal local kernel. It must jointly realize all virtual edges, terminate with finite rational tables, induce exactly \(G^S\), and use \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}\) only through \(\mathrm{lem:exactification\text{-}preserves\text{-}laws}\). The positive-binary two-virtual-edge instance is separately unresolved; only a support-deficient separator and two no-go subclasses are established.

defs.def:certificate-checker: Given \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) and \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}\) first validates finite-table completeness, rational probability normalization and nonnegativity, the product-factor interpretation of mutual independence, and exact induced-graph equality: \(P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) for every vertex, and \(v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S\) exactly when some declared latent scope contains both endpoints. For each \(i\in\{0,1\}\), exhaustive enumeration of the \(R(E_i)\) joint latent assignments computes exact unnormalized selected atoms \(a_i(v)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(V=v,S=1)\) and \(z_i=\sum_{v\in\{0,1\}^V}a_i(v)\). The checker requires \(a_i(v)>0\) and \(a_0(v)z_1=a_1(v)z_0\) for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^V\). It then replaces the structural tables for \(X\) by \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), enumerates again to obtain exact postintervention selected masses \(b_i(y)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(Y=y,S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x_{\mathrm{bin}}))\) and \(q_i=\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^Y}b_i(y)\), and accepts exactly when \(q_0q_1>0\) and \(b_0(y)q_1\ne b_1(y)q_0\) for some \(y\in\{0,1\}^Y\). For a universal implementation constant \(c\), this procedure uses at most \(c\{|V|^2+L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}\) exact rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations.
defs.def:certscm-encoding: \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) consists of finite strings \(E=((\mathcal U_j,p_j,I_j)_{j=1}^m,(P_v,f_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}})\). Each \(\mathcal U_j\) is a nonempty finite latent support, \(p_j:\mathcal U_j\to\mathbb Q\cap[0,1]\) is a complete normalized rational probability table, and \(I_j\subseteq V\cup\{S\}\) declares every endogenous mechanism receiving latent factor \(U_j\); distinct factors are interpreted independently with joint mass \(\prod_jp_j(u_j)\). Each \(P_v\) is the declared observed-parent interface and each \(f_v\) is a complete deterministic table from the states of \(P_v\) and the incident latent factors to \(\{0,1\}\). Exact graph compatibility requires \(P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) for every \(v\), and for every distinct \(v,w\), \(v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S\) if and only if \(\{v,w\}\subseteq I_j\) for at least one \(j\). Thus every listed directed parent occurs in the declared interface, no unlisted directed parent occurs, every listed bidirected edge has a declared shared factor, and no unlisted vertex pair shares a factor. The induced selected atom \(P_{\llbracket E\rrbracket}(V=z,S=1)\) must be positive for every \(z\in\{0,1\}^V\), and a scope \(I_j\) may contain arbitrarily many mechanisms.
defs.def:inverse-lift-handle: For a terminal call descended from \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(D_i,T_i^{(0)},Q_{P_{\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}}}^S[T_i^{(0)}])\) on the exact induced graph \(G^S\), with \(C=D_i\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\) and \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}\) takes a record \((F_0,F_1,R,\overline M_0,\overline M_1,x_{\mathrm{bin}})\in\mathsf{ProjHedgeInput}(G^S;X,Y;C,T)\). It collects in one incidence hypergraph every original bidirected path through \(A_S\cup\{S\}\) that realizes an edge of \(F_1\), introduces jointly rational parameters of mutually independent finite latent factors that may each enter several endogenous mechanisms and all ancestor mechanisms, imposes equality of every binary-signature selected atom before normalization together with preservation of the common projected observational kernel and the nonzero contrast \(\overline Q^{(0)}_{C,x_N}-\overline Q^{(1)}_{C,x_N}\), eliminates shared or branching ancestor mechanisms in a topological order, and searches the remaining rational nullspace for a lift retaining that local contrast. It then applies \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}\) to complete every declared parent interface and bidirected latent incidence. Its target object is an effective inverse-lift constructor producing \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), with accepted exact checker evidence and realized models whose induced graph equals \(G^S\).

thm:executable-success-or-certificate.proof_tex: The recursion assertions are \(\mathrm{lem:sid\text{-}graph\text{-}recursion\text{-}termination}\). For supplied \(E_0,E_1\), \(\mathrm{def:certificate\text{-}checker}\) exhaustively enumerates finite latent, observational, and outcome cells and has the displayed operation bound. By \(\mathrm{lem:certificate\text{-}checker\text{-}soundness}\), acceptance places both realizations in \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), proves equality and positivity of their selected laws, and proves target inequality at \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\). Neither premise constructs a certificate, so no totality conclusion follows.

snapshot.stmt:
For every finite augmented ADMG \(G^S\) with childless \(S\), whenever published Algorithm 1 reaches its single-component recursion, every call chain terminates. Its chain rooted at \(T_i^{(0)}\) has at most \(|T_i^{(0)}|\) invocations, the recursion depth is at most \(\max_i|T_i^{(0)}|\le|N_S|\), and the total number of single-component invocations is at most \(B_0\). Independently, for any supplied \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), the exact NONID checker terminates within
\[
 c\{|V|^2+L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}
\]
exact rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations. If it accepts, the realized models induce exactly \(G^S\), have the same strictly positive selected law, and have unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. This theorem proves graph-recursion termination and certificate-verification soundness only; it does not assert that either failure branch can always compile such a certificate or that \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) is total.

For each \(i\in\{0,1\}\), exhaustive enumeration of the \(R(E_i)\) joint latent assignments computes exact unnormalized selected atoms \(a_i(v)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(V=v,S=1)\) and \(z_i=\sum_{v\in\{0,1\}^V}a_i(v)\). The checker requires \(a_i(v)>0\) and \(a_0(v)z_1=a_1(v)z_0\) for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^V\). It then replaces the structural tables for \(X\) by \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), enumerates again to obtain exact postintervention selected masses \(b_i(y)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(Y=y,S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x_{\mathrm{bin}}))\) and \(q_i=\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^Y}b_i(y)\), and accepts exactly when \(q_0q_1>0\) and \(b_0(y)q_1\ne b_1(y)q_0\) for some \(y\in\{0,1\}^Y\). For a universal implementation constant \(c\), this procedure uses at most \(c\{|V|^2+L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}\) exact rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations.

prop:latent-free-regression.proof_tex:
Assume that \(G^S\) has no bidirected edges and that \(S\) has no children.  Fix \(H\subseteq N_S\), and write
\[
  J_H=G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}].
\]
Taking an induced subgraph cannot create an edge, so \(J_H\) has no bidirected edges.  A district is a maximal set joined by bidirected paths.  A bidirected path between two distinct vertices contains a bidirected edge; hence every district of \(J_H\) is a singleton.  Definition \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}component}\) therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)
 &=\bigl\{K\cap H:K\in\mathcal D(J_H),\ K\cap H\ne\varnothing\bigr\}\\
 &=\bigl\{\{h\}:h\in H\bigr\}. \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]
When \(H=\varnothing\), both sides of (1) are the empty partition, so (1) covers every \(H\subseteq N_S\).

We next exclude an S-Hedge directly from the definitions.  Suppose for contradiction that \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\) holds.  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\),
\[
 C\subsetneq T\subseteq N_S,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)=\{T\}. \tag{2}
\]
The declared type of \(C\) makes \(C\) nonempty, so choose \(t\in C\).  Since \(t\in T\), (1) applied with \(H=T\) says that \(\{t\}\) is a block of \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(T)\).  Combining this fact with (2) yields \(\{t\}=T\).  The inclusions \(\varnothing\ne C\subseteq T=\{t\}\) then force \(C=T\), contradicting \(C\subsetneq T\).  Thus
\[
  \neg\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)
  \quad\text{for every admissible pair }(C,T). \tag{3}
\]

Definition \(\mathrm{def:success\text{-}or\text{-}certificate\text{-}algorithm}\) states that a terminal recursive failure supplies sets \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq N_S\) such that both are single S-components and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\).  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:s\text{-}hedge}\), those conditions are exactly \(\operatorname{SHedge}_{G^S}(C,T)\).  This contradicts (3), so the recursive S-Hedge failure branch of \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) cannot occur.  This argument proves the singleton-component and no-failure conclusions internally; it does not borrow them from the citation.

For the remaining graphical comparison, \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}dag\text{-}sid\text{-}consistency}\) records the precise DAG specialization of AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID Theorem 5.1 and the paragraph immediately following Remark 5.2: the auxiliary effect is always s-ID, while the original selected causal effect is s-ID exactly when the paper's Equation (5), its initial selected d-separation condition, holds; the authors call this consistent with AboueiEtAl2024SID Theorem 2.  This is a comparison of graphical criteria and does not assert literal equality of the two papers' displayed formulas.

It remains to verify the identifying claim as an equality between the observed-law functional and the causal target.  Fix a finite signature \(\sigma\), an intervention value \(x\in\mathcal X_X\), and a model \(M\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:target\text{-}support}\),
\[
  P_M\bigl(S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x)\bigr)>0, \tag{4}
\]
so the intervention-before-conditioning law \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)\) is defined.  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\),
\[
  P_M(V=v,S=1)>0
  \quad\text{for every }v\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j. \tag{5}
\]
Summing (5) over the nonempty finite state space of \(V\) gives \(P_M(S=1)>0\), and hence
\[
  P_{M,\sigma}^S(v)
  =\frac{P_M(V=v,S=1)}{P_M(S=1)}>0. \tag{6}
\]
More generally, for any \(Z\subseteq V\) and \(z\in\mathcal X_Z\), finiteness of the signature and (6) give
\[
  P_{M,\sigma}^S(Z=z)
  =\sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V:\,v|_Z=z}P_{M,\sigma}^S(v)>0, \tag{7}
\]
because the set of completions of \(z\) is nonempty and every summand is positive.  Thus every observed-coordinate conditioning denominator used in the outer conditional and in the successful finite recursive selected-kernel construction is positive.

Now suppose published Algorithm 1 succeeds.  Its soundness theorem, recorded as \(\mathrm{lem:published\text{-}latent\text{-}sid\text{-}soundness}\), applies because of (4)--(7).  Using Definition \(\mathrm{def:eq23\text{-}functional}\), it yields, for every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\),
\[
 \Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_{M,\sigma}^S)(y)
 =P_M\bigl(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),S=1\bigr)
 =\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M)(y). \tag{8}
\]
Since \(\mathcal X_Y\) is finite, the pointwise equalities in (8) imply equality of probability laws.

Finally, let \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)\) have the same selected observational law \(P_{M_0,\sigma}^S=P_{M_1,\sigma}^S=p\).  Applying (8) to each model gives
\[
  \Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_0)
  =\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(p)
  =\Theta_{x,\sigma}(M_1). \tag{9}
\]
Therefore the explicit observed-law map \(p\mapsto\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(p)\) identifies \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}\) whenever Algorithm 1 succeeds, as claimed.

snapshot.stmt: Known-case regression corollary. If \(G^S\) has no bidirected edges and \(S\) has no children, then for every \(H\subseteq N_S\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)\) is the singleton partition of \(H\), and no recursive S-Hedge exists. Consequently the recursive S-Hedge failure branch of \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) cannot occur. The latent-paper criterion reduces to its initial selected d-separation condition, which the published paper states is consistent with the fully observed S-ID criterion. Whenever the latent Algorithm 1 succeeds, its returned \(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}\) identifies \(\Theta_{x,\sigma}\) by published soundness. This corollary does not assert byte-for-byte equality of the two papers' displayed formulas.

defs.def:eq23-functional: For every finite signature \(\sigma\) and every outcome value \(y=(y_S,y_N)\in\prod_{v\in Y}\mathcal X_v\), Eq. 23 is the pointwise functional \[\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma}(P_\sigma^S)(y)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal X_W} P_\sigma^S(Y_S=y_S,W=w\mid X_S=x_S)\sum_{d_{D\setminus Y_N}\in\mathcal X_{D\setminus Y_N}}\prod_{D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)}Q_{P_\sigma,x_N}^S[D_i]\bigl(d_i\mid y_S,w,x_S,d_{D\setminus D_i}\bigr).\] Every factor is produced by a successful single-component recursion and, at every recursion level, is evaluated at \(X_N=x_N\); the outer conditional is evaluated at \(X_S=x_S\).
defs.def:model-class: For every finite signature \(\sigma=(\mathcal X_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}}\) with \(2\le|\mathcal X_v|<\infty\) for \(v\in V\) and \(\mathcal X_S=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathfrak M_+(G^S,\sigma)=\{M:M\text{ has endogenous signature }\sigma,\ M\text{ is a recursive augmented SCM with mutually independent exogenous variables, }\operatorname{Pa}_M(v)=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\text{ for every }v,\ v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal U_M^v\cap\mathcal U_M^w\ne\varnothing\text{ for every distinct }v,w,\text{ and }P_M(V=z,S=1)>0\text{ for every }z\in\prod_{j\in V}\mathcal X_j\}\).
defs.def:s-component: For every \(H\subseteq N_S\), \(\operatorname{SComp}_{G^S}(H)=\{K\cap H:K\in\mathcal D(G^S[H\cup A_S\cup\{S\}]),\ K\cap H\ne\varnothing\}\), where \(\mathcal D\) denotes the district partition.
defs.def:success-or-certificate-algorithm: \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\) runs published Algorithm 1 on a finite augmented ADMG \(G^S\) with childless \(S\), interpreted as the exact graph induced by the SCM parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences, and records \(\mathcal I_0\). Given any finite signature \(\sigma\), on success at intervention value \(x\in\mathcal X_X\) it returns \(\operatorname{ID}(\Phi_{23,x}^{\sigma})\). If the initial d-separation check fails it chooses \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}^{X}\) and returns \(\operatorname{NONID}(x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1,\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}=\mathrm{accept};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), where \((E_0,E_1)=\mathsf{AncestorPair}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) and both certificates induce exactly \(G^S\). If the call rooted at \(D_i\in\mathcal D_S(D)\) reaches a terminal failure \(\operatorname{sID\text{-}Single}(C,T,Q_{P_\sigma}^S[T])\), then \(C=D_i\), \(C\subsetneq T\subseteq T_i^{(0)}\), both \(C\) and \(T\) are single S-components, and \(\operatorname{An}_{G^S[T]}(C)=T\); the algorithm chooses \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\) and returns the same encoded \(\operatorname{NONID}\) object with \((E_0,E_1)=\mathsf{SHedgePair}(G^S,C,T,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\). This total failure branch is enabled only by a proved effective inverse-lift constructor returning rational exact-graph \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) objects; an existential arbitrary-SCM lift does not implement \(\mathsf{sID}^{\pm}\). The trace stores the multiset rank before and after every recursive call.

prop:ukb-conditional-feasibility-audit.proof_tex:
Fix \(\sigma_{EI}\), \(G^{EI}\), \(\mathcal O\), and \(a\) as in the statement, and abbreviate
\[
 \mathfrak M=\mathfrak M_{EI,+}(G^{EI},\sigma_{EI}),
 \qquad
 \mathcal F=\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI}).
\]
We first verify that every conditional law used below is well defined.  If \(N\in\mathfrak M\), then, by \(\mathrm{ass:exposure\text{-}selector\text{-}positivity}\), \(\mathrm{ass:imaging\text{-}selector\text{-}positivity}\), and \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}selector\text{-}model\text{-}class}\), for each \(r\in\{E,I\}\) and each substantive cell \(v\),
\[
 P_N(V_{EI}=v,S_r=1)>0.
\]
Because the signature is finite and its product state space is nonempty, summation over all substantive cells gives
\[
 P_N(S_r=1)
 =\sum_{v\in\prod_{k\in V_{EI}}\mathcal X_k}
   P_N(V_{EI}=v,S_r=1)>0.
\]
Thus both components of \(\operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(N)\), as defined in \(\mathrm{def:tian\text{-}observation\text{-}map}\), exist.  Moreover,
\[
 P_N(A=a,S_I=1)
 =\sum_{v:v_A=a}P_N(V_{EI}=v,S_I=1)>0.
\]
The model is recursive by \(\mathrm{ass:two\text{-}selector\text{-}exact\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}selector\text{-}model\text{-}class}\).  For any exogenous realization at which the observational solution has \(A=a\), replacing the structural equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\) leaves the entire solution unchanged: this follows by induction along a topological ordering, since the replacement agrees with the observational value at \(A\), and every later structural function receives the same parent values and the same exogenous inputs.  Consequently
\[
 \{A=a,S_I=1\}_{\mathrm{obs}}
 \subseteq
 \{S_I=1\}_{\operatorname{do}(A=a)},
\]
and hence
\[
 P_N(S_I=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))
 \ge P_N(A=a,S_I=1)>0.
\]
Therefore \(\Theta^I_a(N)=P_N(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),S_I=1)\), with intervention performed before conditioning as specified by the symbol \(\Theta^I_a\), is also well defined.

We now separate the causal target from the observation map.  Point identification of \(\Theta^I_a\) from the two Tian margins over \(\mathfrak M\) means the following property:
\[
 \mathsf{Id}_{EI}(a)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{for all }N_0,N_1\in\mathfrak M,
 \quad
 \operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(N_0)=\operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(N_1)
 \Longrightarrow
 \Theta^I_a(N_0)=\Theta^I_a(N_1).
\]
This line is the definition of identification relative to the stated observation map; it does not define the causal target, which was defined independently by intervention followed by conditioning.

Suppose that the audit exhibits \(M_{EI,0},M_{EI,1}\in\mathcal F\) with
\[
 \Theta^I_a(M_{EI,0})\ne\Theta^I_a(M_{EI,1}).
\]
Unfolding \(\mathrm{def:tian\text{-}feasibility\text{-}fiber}\) separately for \(j=0,1\) yields
\[
 M_{EI,j}\in\mathfrak M
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(M_{EI,j})=\mathcal O.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(M_{EI,0})
 =\mathcal O
 =\operatorname{Obs}_{EI}(M_{EI,1}),
\]
whereas their causal targets differ.  The pair therefore falsifies the universal implication defining \(\mathsf{Id}_{EI}(a)\), so
\[
 \neg\mathsf{Id}_{EI}(a).
\]
This proves nonidentification from the two observed margins over the positive exact-graph two-selector class.

The same membership statements also prove \(\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\).  Furthermore, by \(\mathrm{ass:two\text{-}selector\text{-}exact\text{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}selector\text{-}model\text{-}class}\), each displayed model has exactly the parent interfaces of \(G^{EI}\), and two distinct endogenous mechanisms share an exogenous input if and only if their vertices are joined by a bidirected edge of \(G^{EI}\).  Thus permitted edges are not being silently deleted or added.  By \(\mathrm{def:tian\text{-}imaging\text{-}law\text{-}set}\), the full imaging-selected laws compatible with the two margins are exactly
\[
 \Gamma_I(\mathcal O;G^{EI})
 =\{P_N(V_{EI}\mid S_I=1):N\in\mathcal F\},
\]
which is the set recorded by the audit.

Finally, unfold \(\mathrm{def:tian\text{-}feasibility\text{-}audit}\).  Its nonidentification branch is enabled only by two displayed models in the same fiber whose \(\Theta^I_a\)-values differ.  If no such pair is displayed, that definition permits only an unmet-assumptions report identifying additional fusion or selected-instrument assumptions, or an inconclusive output.  A one-selector \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) pair with a common law \(P(V\mid S=1)\) does not, merely from that fact, instantiate the two quantifiers in \(\mathsf{Id}_{EI}(a)\): its members have not thereby been shown to lie in \(\mathfrak M\), and equality of one common selected law has not thereby been shown to equal the ordered two-selector observation \(\mathcal O\).  Separate verification that both realized models belong to the same \(\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI})\) is therefore a necessary condition for that pair to serve as a certificate for the Tian margins.  This proves every asserted branch of the proposition.

snapshot.stmt: Fix a finite two-selector signature \(\sigma_{EI}\), an exact induced graph \(G^{EI}\), an observed pair \(\mathcal O=(P(Z,A,L\mid S_E=1),P(Z,Y,L\mid S_I=1))\), and \(a\in\mathcal X_A\). If \(\mathsf{Audit}_{EI}\) exhibits \(M_{EI,0},M_{EI,1}\in\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI})\) with \(\Theta^I_a(M_{EI,0})\ne\Theta^I_a(M_{EI,1})\), then the imaging-selected HbA1c intervention target is not identified from those two observed Tian margins over the positive exact-graph two-selector class. Such membership establishes that the fiber is nonempty and that both models have exactly the declared parent interfaces and shared-latent incidences. The audit may return a UK Biobank data-compatible nonidentification conclusion only with this same-fiber pair. Otherwise it returns only unmet fusion or selected-instrument assumptions, or an inconclusive result. In particular, a generic one-selector \(\operatorname{CertSCM}\) pair with one common full selected law is not a certificate for the two Tian margins unless both realized models are separately verified to belong to the same \(\mathcal F_{EI}(\mathcal O;G^{EI})\) fiber.

defs.def:ancestor-pair: \(\mathsf{AncestorPair}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}};\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})=(E_0,E_1)\) applies the positive rational binary countermodel construction from the complete fully observed S-ID necessity proof on \(A_S\cup\{S\}\), extends the same rational mechanisms to every nonancestor vertex, records the result as a pair in \(\operatorname{RawCertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\), and applies \(\operatorname{Exactify}_{G^S}\) to both members. The returned certificates have every declared parent interface and shared-latent incidence required for their induced graph to equal \(G^S\), and include evidence that \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}(G^S,X,Y,x_{\mathrm{bin}},E_0,E_1)=\mathrm{accept}\).
defs.def:certificate-checker: Given \(E_0,E_1\in\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) and \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), \(\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{NONID}}\) first validates finite-table completeness, rational probability normalization and nonnegativity, the product-factor interpretation of mutual independence, and exact induced-graph equality: \(P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) for every vertex, and \(v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S\) exactly when some declared latent scope contains both endpoints. For each \(i\in\{0,1\}\), exhaustive enumeration of the \(R(E_i)\) joint latent assignments computes exact unnormalized selected atoms \(a_i(v)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(V=v,S=1)\) and \(z_i=\sum_{v\in\{0,1\}^V}a_i(v)\). The checker requires \(a_i(v)>0\) and \(a_0(v)z_1=a_1(v)z_0\) for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^V\). It then replaces the structural tables for \(X\) by \(x_{\mathrm{bin}}\), enumerates again to obtain exact postintervention selected masses \(b_i(y)=P_{\llbracket E_i\rrbracket}(Y=y,S=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x_{\mathrm{bin}}))\) and \(q_i=\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^Y}b_i(y)\), and accepts exactly when \(q_0q_1>0\) and \(b_0(y)q_1\ne b_1(y)q_0\) for some \(y\in\{0,1\}^Y\). For a universal implementation constant \(c\), this procedure uses at most \(c\{|V|^2+L(E_0)+L(E_1)+2^{|V|}(R(E_0)+R(E_1))(|V|+|Y|+1)\}\) exact rational arithmetic and table-lookup operations.
defs.def:certscm-encoding: \(\operatorname{CertSCM}(G^S,\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}})\) consists of finite strings \(E=((\mathcal U_j,p_j,I_j)_{j=1}^m,(P_v,f_v)_{v\in V\cup\{S\}})\). Each \(\mathcal U_j\) is a nonempty finite latent support, \(p_j:\mathcal U_j\to\mathbb Q\cap[0,1]\) is a complete normalized rational probability table, and \(I_j\subseteq V\cup\{S\}\) declares every endogenous mechanism receiving latent factor \(U_j\); distinct factors are interpreted independently with joint mass \(\prod_jp_j(u_j)\). Each \(P_v\) is the declared observed-parent interface and each \(f_v\) is a complete deterministic table from the states of \(P_v\) and the incident latent factors to \(\{0,1\}\). Exact graph compatibility requires \(P_v=\operatorname{Pa}_{G^S}(v)\) for every \(v\), and for every distinct \(v,w\), \(v\leftrightarrow w\in G^S\) if and only if \(\{v,w\}\subseteq I_j\) for at least one \(j\). Thus every listed directed parent occurs in the declared interface, no unlisted directed parent occurs, every listed bidirected edge has a declared shared factor, and no unlisted vertex pair shares a factor. The induced selected atom \(P_{\llbracket E\rrbracket}(V=z,S=1)\) must be positive for every \(z\in\{0,1\}^V\), and a scope \(I_j\) may contain arbitrarily many mechanisms.

prose_overlay.tldr: For graphs satisfying \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\), published latent S-ID Algorithm 1 succeeds if and only if the selected causal query is graphwise identifiable over the full positive exact-graph augmented-SCM class, with models compared only within one finite signature. Success returns Abouei et al.'s Eq. 23 functional. A terminal recursive failure contains an ordinary hedge whose edges are actual edges of \(G^S[N_S]\); Shpitser--Pearl's hedge criterion and KivvaEtAl2022's positive finite-state construction give a full-support multistate separator, and a common randomized-response routing plus finite exactification yields two exact-graph models with the same strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. Separate finite rank bounds certify graph recursion, and the rational checker is sound for any supplied certificate. The result does not construct binary or rational failure witnesses. Universal virtual-edge completeness, the positive-binary two-virtual-edge separator, initial selected-d-separation failure construction, exact-rational inverse lifting, and total success-or-certificate compilation remain open. The UK Biobank component remains only a conditional two-selector feasibility audit.
prose_overlay.related_work: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID defines latent subpopulation S-ID, Algorithm 1, S-components, S-Hedges, and Eq. 23, proves soundness, and leaves completeness open. This paper advances that frontier only on \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\): it does not settle unrestricted terminal traces or initial selected-d-separation failure. ShpitserPearl2006 provides Definition 7's ordinary hedge criterion and Theorem 4's nonidentifiability implication. KivvaEtAl2022, not KivvaEtAl2023 Appendix A.1.1, provides the positive finite-state ordinary-ID substrate used here; the new work is the reduction from an actual-edge terminal S-Hedge to that substrate, followed by selected-law extension, actual-edge root-to-outcome routing, and inert exactification. KivvaEtAl2023 concerns conditional generalized identification and does not directly state this ordinary-forest specialization. HuangValtorta2008 and TianPearl2002 provide the ordinary recursive-identification and district-factorization background. AboueiEtAl2024SID is used only for the known no-latent DAG regression check. ChenZoeterMooij2024 explains selection conditioning as an SCM transformation but does not supply a common-selected-law inverse countermodel lift. RichardsonEtAl2017 supplies nested Markov and district-kernel language useful for describing recursive kernels and full-graph extension; it does not prove the selected-law converse. BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022 studies semiparametric inference after hidden-variable identification and is relevant only to separating this population identification result from downstream estimation; it supplies no completeness claim. LeeGhassamiShpitser2024 uses multiple systematic-selection inputs rather than one full selected law. DuarteEtAl2024AutoBounds addresses optimization-based discrete partial identification, not singleton collapse at S-ID success. The UK Biobank citations motivate a conditional two-selector feasibility audit only; no empirical effect or unconditional fusion claim is made.
prose_overlay.interpretation: The native theorem marks the boundary at which terminal latent S-ID failure already contains an ordinary hedge inside the selection-nonancestor graph. At that boundary, an ordinary positive separator can be passed through a common independent selector and sufficiently accurate full-support channels without canceling its root contrast. When a terminal forest uses virtual edges through ancestors of \(S\), this argument no longer controls the selected-law normalizer, so the universal converse remains unresolved.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: The proof requires actual-edge nested forests on every reachable terminal failure. It does not realize projected virtual bidirected edges through shared or branching ancestors of \(S\). Accordingly, unrestricted graphwise completeness, the positive-binary two-virtual-edge separation problem, the initial selected-d-separation failure constructor, exact-rational inverse lifting, and total success-or-certificate compilation all remain open. The proved Kivva reduction is finite and full-support but multistate; no binary reduction, rational parameter choice, or executable constructor follows from it. The rational checker theorem is only a sound verification result conditional on a certificate being supplied.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The headline theorem is an if-and-only-if result only for finite childless-selector queries satisfying \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\). The compatible class is the full positive recursive augmented-SCM class whose declared observed-parent interfaces and shared-exogenous incidences induce exactly \(G^S\), and observational equivalence compares models only within one finite signature. On success, Eq. 23 is evaluated at \(X_S=x_S\) in the outer conditional and at \(X_N=x_N\) in every recursive selected kernel. On a terminal native failure, the proof supplies one finite multistate exact-graph pair with a common strictly positive selected law and unequal intervention-before-conditioning targets. It does not supply a binary or rational pair. Coordinate-constant exactification preserves the relevant laws under the declared-interface graph convention. Graph-recursion bounds and sound finite checking of a supplied rational certificate are separate proved properties; they do not make the failure branch executable. Universal virtual-edge completeness, the positive-binary two-virtual-edge separator, initial-check failure construction, exact-rational inverse lifting, and total compilation remain open. The no-bidirected-edge result is only a published-case regression check. The UK Biobank component is conditional on a specified two-selector graph and a nonempty feasibility fiber; absent two exact-graph models in that same fiber with unequal targets, it reports only unmet assumptions or an inconclusive audit, not data-compatible nonidentification.

project_justification.gap: AboueiEtAl2024LatentSID proves Algorithm 1 sound and leaves completeness open. Ordinary hedge completeness alone does not solve terminal failures whose projected bidirected edges must be realized through shared or branching ancestors of \(S\), because such realizations can change every selected atom and its normalizer. KivvaEtAl2022 supplies a positive finite-state construction for ordinary identification failures, but not a selected-law inverse lift through those virtual edges.
project_justification.niche: The predicate \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\) isolates the terminal traces for which the nested common-root forests can be chosen using actual directed and bidirected edges of \(G^S[N_S]\). On this class the ordinary positive-forest construction can be used before adding a common selection mechanism and actual-edge root-to-outcome channels.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the missing converse on \(\operatorname{NativeForestTrace}(G^S;X,Y)\). It verifies the Shpitser--Pearl hedge clauses for each terminal native forest, invokes KivvaEtAl2022 for finite full-support ordinary countermodels, extracts a nonzero root-atom contrast, routes it to \(Y_N\) through common full-support randomized-response channels on treatment-avoiding actual paths, and exactifies inert interfaces without changing the equal selected law or target contrast. Combined with published soundness, this gives the success-if-and-only-if theorem and Eq. 23 on success. Independent results bound the graph recursion and verify any supplied rational certificate, without claiming a binary, rational, or executable failure constructor.
